note: Real-meaning lines. Edit freely: changes here never trigger a Netlify deploy. A line is not reused within 14 days in either country.
rules: deceptively spacious
It's small. They know it's small.
Spacious in the way a phone box is spacious.
The deception is the spacious bit.
Wide-angle lens doing overtime.
\bbijou\b
You can touch both walls from the sofa.
French for "where does the bed go".
Bijou. Like a shoebox, but posher.
\bcompact\b
Tiny. Measure your bed first.
Compact. The hoover lives in the shower.
One of you will have to sleep standing up.
Compact, as in you can cook from bed.
\bcos(y|ie)\b
Small. Very, very small.
Cosy means you will hear each other think.
Two people is cosy. Three is a fire hazard.
Cosy. Agent for "the sofa won't fit".

in need of (some |full |complete )?(modernisation|modernization|refurbishment|renovation|updating|upgrading|tlc)|requires? (some |full )?(modernisation|modernization|refurbishment|updating|upgrading)|\btlc\b
Bring a skip. Bring two.
Needs updating. The wiring remembers dial-up.
TLC means a builder, a plumber and a priest.
The kitchen is older than you.
(huge|great|enormous|excellent|tremendous|exciting) potential
It's a wreck with a garden.
Potential is what you call a problem you haven't costed.
Excellent potential means the current state is not excellent.
The potential is mostly in the skip.
Potential. Also known as a quote you can't afford.
renovation project|refurbishment project|doer[- ]upper
It's a wreck. They've said so politely.
Project, as in your next five years.
Doer-upper. The doing is all yours.
(grade (ii|2)|listed building|listed property)
You'll need the council's permission to change a lightbulb.
Listed. Double glazing is a planning offence.
Historic. So is the plumbing.
(much[- ]loved|cherished|lovingly maintained) (family )?home
Nobody has touched it since 1987.
Much loved. Not much updated.
The carpet has seen three generations and a dog.
Cherished. The avocado bathroom suite especially.
Lovingly maintained. The wallpaper was loved most.
(original|period) features
Original windows. Bring a jumper.
Period features, including period draughts.
The fireplace works. The heating does not.
Original features. Original wiring too, probably.
Coving, ceiling roses and a boiler from 1979.
Period features. The radiators clank like a ghost.
\bcharacter(ful)?\b|full of charm|charming
Nothing in it is level.
Charm is what old houses have instead of insulation.
Character means a ghost or a damp patch.
Charming. Drop a marble and watch it roll.
Character. Every stair creaks in a different key.
Charming, like an uncle who won't leave.
low[- ]maintenance (rear |back |front )?garden
It's concrete.
Low maintenance. Gravel and a wheelie bin.
The garden is a patio with ambition.
(stunning|breathtaking|panoramic|uninterrupted) (sea |mountain |coastal |countryside )?views
The photo was taken from the one good window.
The view is great from the attic, standing on a chair.
Uninterrupted views until someone builds in front.
rarely (available|come|comes)|rare opportunity|unique opportunity|opportunity not to be missed
The last owner lasted 40 years. Ask why.
Rare opportunity. Every listing is a rare opportunity.
Not to be missed. Then missed by everyone for six months.
Rarely available, because nobody could afford it.
no onward chain|chain[- ]free|vacant possession
They've already moved out. They want this over.
Chain-free. The vendor is already in Spain.
Nobody lives here. Nobody wanted to.
investment opportunity|ideal for investors?|investors? (will|take note)
Currently tenanted. Possibly by students.
Ideal for investors. Not for anyone living in it.
Investment opportunity. The yield is on paper.
(ideal|perfect|excellent) (for )?(first[- ]time buyers?|starter home|first home)
Two bedrooms if you count the box room.
Starter home. You'll be starting over in three years.
First-time buyer. Second mortgage.
walk[- ]in condition|turn[- ]?key|move[- ]in ready|ready to move into
They painted it magnolia last week.
Walk-in condition. Walk round the cracks.
Move-in ready, if you like grey.
Turnkey. Every room is the same shade of greige.
Ready to move into. Just bring your own personality.
(immaculate|pristine|beautifully presented|presented in excellent)
Staged by someone with more cushions than you.
Immaculate. They hid everything in the attic.
Beautifully presented by a man with a ring light.
The fruit bowl is plastic.
Presented beautifully. Lived in by nobody.
Every surface is clear. Where do they keep the toaster?
(quiet|peaceful|tranquil|secluded) (cul[- ]de[- ]sac|location|setting|road|lane|position)
There's one bus a day. It doesn't stop here.
Quiet. The nearest shop is a twenty-minute drive.
Secluded. The postman needs a map.
Tranquil. Broadband is a rumour.
Peaceful. Until the neighbour gets a leaf blower.
(idyllic|picturesque|rural|countryside) (setting|location|village|surroundings)
You'll need a car. And a second car.
Picturesque. Pints are a taxi away.
Rural. Your nearest neighbour is a cow.
(village|town) centre|main street|high street location
Above, beside or behind a chipper.
Town centre. Closing time is your alarm clock.
Main street. The smoking area is your front step.
convenient(ly)? (located |situated )?(for|to) (the )?(local )?(amenities|shops|transport|bus|train|rail|motorway|m50|city)
You'll hear the traffic from bed.
Convenient for the bus. The bus stop is your wall.
Handy for the shops. The car park is out the back.
Close to amenities. The amenity is a Spar.
(close to|minutes from|easy access to) (the )?(m50|m\d+|n\d+|motorway|dual carriageway|ring road)
You'll hear the motorway from bed.
Easy motorway access. The motorway has easy access to you.
Minutes from the motorway. Minutes, not metres. Hopefully.
(south|west)[- ]facing (rear |back )?garden
The garden gets sun for one hour in June.
South-facing. The weather has not been told.
West-facing. The barbecue gets used twice a year.
open[- ]plan
They knocked a wall down. Hopefully not that one.
Open plan. Every room smells of dinner.
Open plan. Nowhere to hide from anyone.
The telly, the kettle and the kids, all in one room.
Open plan. The extractor fan is now the loudest thing in your life.
(attic|loft) conversion|converted (attic|loft)
Mind your head. Always mind your head.
Converted attic. Ask if it had planning.
Loft room. Stand in the middle only.
\bcottage\b
Mind your head on the beams.
Cottage. The doors were built for hobbits.
Roses round the door, damp up the wall.
architect[- ]designed|contemporary (home|design|residence)|floor[- ]to[- ]ceiling
Floor-to-ceiling windows. Floor-to-ceiling heating bills.
Architect-designed. Nowhere to put a wardrobe.
Contemporary. The neighbours objected.
\bbungalow\b
It's all on one level. That's the whole pitch.
Bungalow. The garden is bigger than the house.
Bungalow. Every retiree in the county is bidding.
(online )?auction|\bamv\b|guide price|offers (in excess of|over)
The guide price is a suggestion. A low one.
Auction. Bring cash and a strong heart.
Offers over. Way over.
new[- ]build|newly built|a[- ]?rated|nzeb
The walls are thinner than the brochure.
New build. The snag list is longer than the deeds.
New build. The trees in the photo are digital.
mid[- ]terrace|terraced (house|home)
You'll know your neighbours' TV schedule.
Terraced. The bins go through the house.
Mid-terrace. You share a wall and an opinion.
popular (residential )?(area|estate|development|location)|much sought|sought[- ]after
You're paying for the address, not the house.
Sought after. By everyone with more money than you.
Popular area. Popular with the estate agent.
Ever-popular. Ever-expensive.
Popular. Parking is a blood sport.
Sought after. Mostly by the people already living there.
well[- ]proportioned
The rooms are fine. That's the best they could do.
Well proportioned. Nothing else stood out.
Well proportioned. The agent ran out of adjectives.
(spacious|generous|extensive) (family )?(accommodation|living space|home)
Big. Heating it is your problem.
Spacious. Three floors means you will live on the stairs.
Generous rooms, generous bills.
Plenty of space. None of it warm.
Spacious. Bring shouting.
extended|extension
The extension is where the heat goes to die.
Extended. Ask to see the sign-off.
The extension is a different colour for a reason.
(viewing|viewings) (is |are )?(highly )?(recommended|advised|essential)
The photos aren't doing it any favours.
Viewing essential. The photos are lying.
You have to see it. They can't describe it.
Must be viewed. Because you won't believe the photos.
(cul[- ]de[- ]sac)
Every child on the road will be in your garden.
Cul-de-sac. Every car reverses into your drive.
Cul-de-sac. The residents' WhatsApp never sleeps.
(coastal|seaside|beside the sea|sea views?)
Everything you own will rust. But the view.
Seaside. The seagulls own the bins.
Sea air. Sea damp.
(growing|young) famil(y|ies)
Ideal for the growing family. Until they grow.
Family home. The kids will want their own rooms. They won't get them.
premier|prestigious|exclusive (location|address|development)
Premier location. Premier stamp duty.
Prestigious. The neighbours will tell you so.
Exclusive. The gate code is the whole personality.
log[- ]?burn|wood[- ]?burn|stove
The log burner is the only warm spot. Fight for it.
Wood burner. Your clothes will smell of it forever.
A stove. The rest of the heating is vibes.
three (spacious )?floors|over three (storeys|stories|levels)|townhouse
Three floors. You will live on the stairs.
Townhouse. Your calves will thank you.
(sun|south)[- ]?(room|lounge)|conservatory
The conservatory is an oven in July and a fridge in January.
Sunroom. Used twice a year, to dry clothes.
(garage|outbuilding|shed|workshop)
The garage has never seen a car.
There's a shed. Your partner will live in it.
(en[- ]suite|ensuite)
En suite. A shower in the wardrobe.
Ensuite. Your partner hears everything.

energyBad: Heating bills like a second mortgage.
You can see your breath in the hall.
The radiators are mostly for show.
Wear a coat to bed. Two coats.
energyGood: So airtight you'll need to open a window to sneeze.
A-rated. You will never be cold. You will never be cool either.
Heat-pumped, insulated and sealed. Like a lunchbox.
cheap: There's a reason it's this cheap. Find it.
Cheap. Someone has already tried to fix it.
posh: The stamp duty alone would buy a nice car.
The utility room is bigger than your flat.
bigBeds: Five bedrooms. Four of them are for boxes.
Lots of bedrooms. One bathroom. Good luck.
Big family home. The queue for the shower starts at six.
generic: Every photo was taken with a wide-angle lens.
The best room is the one they didn't photograph.
The agent said "bright" three times in one paragraph.
The neighbours are lovely. The neighbours wrote this.
Great storage, as long as you own nothing.
Recently decorated, as in last Tuesday.
Photographed on the only sunny day of the year.
The bathroom photo is suspiciously close up.
Every light in the house was on for the photos.
The kitchen is "modern". It was modern once.
No photo of the boiler. Draw your own conclusions.
The garden photo is the neighbour's garden.
They mention the parking a lot. That's the selling point.
Lovely house. Shame about the road.
Bright and airy. The windows don't close.
The photos were taken at golden hour. So was the price.
Three photos of the hall. Think about that.
Nice house. The listing is doing a lot of heavy lifting.
The garden is in every photo. The kitchen is in one.
Fresh paint. Ask what it's covering.
A bowl of lemons on the counter. Classic.
Described as "well located". Located, at least.
There's a mirror in every room. The rooms need help.
The agent has never used the word "small" in their life.
Fine house. Nobody writes a poem about fine.
You'll love it. Your survey won't.
The drone shot is doing a lot of work here.
The hot press is the warmest room in the house.
The bedrooms are "double". Just about.
Every room is grey. Even the outside.
The bin storage gets its own photo.
It ticks every box on a form nobody filled in.
Viewing on Saturday. Twenty couples, one stairs.
Lovely. The road outside is a rat run.
There's a utility room. It's a cupboard with a washing machine.
Nothing wrong with it that money can't fix.
The fireplace is fake. The price isn't.
The heating works. The bills work harder.
Plenty of light. And plenty of draughts with it.
Gorgeous kitchen. The rest of the house is jealous.
Parking for two cars. Not your two cars.
The gravel driveway announces every visitor.
Ideal home. Ideal for whom, they don't say.
There's a breakfast bar. Nobody has ever eaten breakfast at it.
The listing mentions "light" eleven times.
Wide hall. Narrow everything else.
The bathroom has been "recently upgraded". With a new shower curtain.
Lots of storage. Mostly under the stairs.
The back garden is lovely. You'll see it from the kitchen sink.
Close to schools. Close to the school run, too.
Good bones. Agent-speak for "everything else needs doing".
The second bedroom is a desk with a door.
The photos skip straight from the hall to the garden.
Neutral décor. Beige in every direction.
Bright reception room. The other rooms are less forthcoming.
Freshly carpeted. Don't look underneath.
The landing is bigger than one of the bedrooms.
Superb location. The house is just there.
Has a downstairs toilet. They're very proud of it.
Every window has a view. Mostly of other windows.
Plenty of kerb appeal. The kerb is the best bit.
The boiler is "serviced annually". Since when, they don't say.
Family home. Bring your own family.
Excellent condition, for its age. Its age is not mentioned.
The agent called it a "gem". The gem is the price tag.
One of those houses that looks better at dusk.
Nice porch. Big electric bill.
There's a playroom. It's the dining room with toys in it.
Very private. The hedge is eight feet tall.
Great for entertaining. If your guests stand.
A home office. Formerly the box room. Still the box room.
There's a view of the park. From the bathroom window.
Sound house. Sound like the neighbours, too.
The kitchen island is bigger than the garden.
Patio doors to the garden. The garden is the patio.
High ceilings. High heating.
They call it a "snug". It's a corridor with a chair.
The extension was done by a cousin.
The front door is the newest thing in the house.
Feature wall. There's always a feature wall.
Recently re-roofed. Ask what happened to the old one.
There's a garden room. It's a shed with a TV.
Close to everything. Including the dual carriageway.
All the rooms are "good sized". None of them are big.
Plenty of parking on the street. Everybody else thinks so too.
